facebook.content_angle: Underwater dolphin kick — how most club swimmers treat the breakout as recovery instead of the fastest phase of every lap, and the drill to fix it
facebook.post_text:
Your fastest speed in the pool isn't on the surface. 🚀

Most club swimmers surface after every turn and start stroking as fast as possible — but they're actually slowing down the moment they break out. The underwater dolphin kick phase is measurably faster than freestyle for almost every swimmer. Yet most treat it like a transition, not a weapon.

👉 Elite swimmers hold their kick for 10–15 metres off every wall
👉 Studies show streamline + dolphin kick outpaces surface swimming by up to 0.3 m/s
👉 That's a potential 1–2 second gain per lap — without touching your stroke at all

The wall gives you free speed. Most swimmers hand it straight back. 💥

✔️ Drill it: push off, hold streamline, count 6 powerful kicks before your first stroke
✔️ Focus on tight body position — any gap in your core kills the momentum
✔️ Train it every rep until the breakout becomes your strongest phase

How many dolphin kicks are you holding off the wall right now?
